summary.one_liner: Goofy is an unofficial macOS desktop wrapper for Facebook Messenger, built as a native Swift/SwiftUI app around a web view of messenger.com.
summary.what_it_does: Goofy shows a web view of facebook.com/messages inside a native macOS window. It injects a small JavaScript snippet into messenger.com to enable macOS notifications when new messages arrive while the app is running. Clicking a notification jumps to that conversation. It also shows the unread message count as a badge on the Dock icon, updating while the app runs. The README says the app is built with macOS's native WebView via Swift and SwiftUI rather than Electron. The source code is on GitHub for review.
use_cases: Run Facebook Messenger as a desktop app on Mac
Get macOS notifications for new Messenger messages
See unread Messenger count on the Dock icon
Use a lightweight Messenger client with low memory use
how_to_run: Download the latest version from the releases page
Move Goofy to the Applications folder
notable: Native Swift/SwiftUI app using macOS WebView, not Electron, so the README says it is smaller and uses less memory
Click a notification to open that Messenger conversation directly
Dock badge shows unread message count
Injects a small JavaScript snippet into messenger.com for notifications and badge counting
caveats: Notifications only work while the Messenger app is open and running
Unofficial client, not affiliated with Facebook or Meta (the listing describes it as unofficial)
The README describes a macOS-only app
